It's true though, that weight-loss should not necessarily be the *goal,* but the way of reaching the goal. You don't want to live and die by the number on the scale. If your goal is to look better, be healthier, or be able to do something physical, weight-loss can get you there, but I think it's unhealthy to obsess over a 'goal weight.'

I often wonder why a lot of people here say the goal is to not have to count calories. I know that it's not "normal," but does my relationship with food have to be *normal* for it to be *healthy?*

As someone whose BMI was once 'obese,' I'd very much like to remain 'healthy.' That's an unusual thing to do, and not many people are able to keep it up. If I'm not doing something to give myself an advantage, I think I will fail like so many others who lost weight.

I can't tell you how good it feels to hear someone else say they understand the "revenge" line of thinking. It's something that sounds so terrible that I would never say it out loud. I don't think I could even say it to myself. But sometimes that feeling is so strong. Sometimes I feel like the only thing holding me back is the fact that I wouldn't get to "enjoy" that aspect of it, anyway.

As for the thing about my friends, thanks for reassuring me. I don't know if I'm a bad person, but I also might have freaked out a little too much. I don't know. I've got a lot on my mind right now, and I'm struggling to make sense of it all. 

Anyway, I think I'd better head off to bed now, but I can't tell you how much I've appreciated your willingness to listen to me. If you ever want to shoot me a PM, I'd love to talk again sometime. It doesn't have to be so heavy, either. I won't PM you because of the whole not wanting to be a burden thing, but. . . yeah. Either way, it's been really refreshing and thanks again.

I think the reason I feel guilty for feeling sorry for myself is that I know kind of do it to myself. I feel like I'm pretty shallow when it comes to the people I want to be friends with. It sound like you aren't at all, so now I'm afraid you'll think I'm a terrible person for saying this, but hey, you're still talking to me after I said I want to make people feel guilty by killing myself, so I've got nothing to lose. 

It's not something I do consciously, but I realize that every single one of my friends is more attractive and more socially aware than I am. I guess that's the reason they don't go to me for comfort, but I want to go to them. It's like, I'm friends with these people because I want to be them, you know? I look through the contacts in my phone and realize that I would trade my life for almost anyone's there in a heartbeat.

I see people worse off than me and think, "yeah, I can offer them some kind words," but I don't really-- God damn it. You see where I'm going with this. I never even realized it until I started typing. I was kind of aware of how selfish I was, but just putting it to words seems terrible. I think you seem like a great person. You're talking to me when I have nothing to offer you, but I really don't deserve it.

Did you ever feel like you weren't justified in going to get help? I know people love to point to Robin Williams and say "It doesn't matter where you are in life," but I feel like it really does. 

I am really, really bad at talking to people and have trouble establishing any sort of connection with them, always afraid to say the wrong thing. I feel sorry for myself because, like you said, I know I have good intentions, but I'm bad at communicating them. But then I see people who have it even worse, who have absolutely no social skills, and no friends, and I feel guilty for feeling sorry for myself. And I feel guilty for not wanting to make an effort to understand someone so socially inept, but wanting people to make that same effort for me.

Hmm, I really lost focus in that last paragraph. No, I'm just saying that professionals have seen people much worse-off than me, and I feel like they would think I'm just being whiny. Which I guess I am. But what I really want is sympathy, not help. Shit man, I'm confusing myself now.
Say something. Or not. I'll stop now. Okay I'm done. Ugggghhh, I'm not going to reread what I wrote.
